what_it_does: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) are AI models that learn from data shaped like a graph — nodes connected by edges — such as social networks or molecular structures. Training a large GNN on multiple graphics cards (GPUs) at once is appealing for speed, but the irregular shape of real graphs means some GPUs end up doing far more work than others (load imbalance), and the GPUs spend a lot of time sending data back and forth (communication overhead). ParGNN addresses both problems: it uses a profiling step to measure where the imbalance lies, then over-partitions the graph into more pieces than there are GPUs so that work can be redistributed more evenly. It also overlaps the computation happening on one partition with the data transfer needed for the next, so GPUs are not sitting idle waiting for data. The paper claims these techniques scale GNN training without sacrificing accuracy.
